s.note: the magic acorns that turn things to stone
s.how: Toast 100g hazelnuts, rub off the skins and chop finely with a handful of chives. Pat 250g bocconcini dry and roll each ball in the hazelnut mix so it looks like a little acorn. Arrange on a plate and drizzle with a little honey.

s.note: Willow's farm in the Nelwyn village
s.how: Mix 500g flour, 7g yeast, a spoon of butter and 300ml warm water to a dough and prove an hour. Shape into rolls and bake at 200C for 18 minutes. Mash butter with chopped parsley and chives and serve the warm rolls with it and a wedge of brie.

m.n: Crossroads tavern beef and root veg stew
m.note: the rowdy tavern where Madmartigan hides
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots and 2 parsnips in chunks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 1 tbsp flour and 2 tbsp tomato paste, then 1L beef stock, thyme and a bay leaf. Cover and simmer for 3 hours until the beef is tender and the sauce is rich. Serve in bowls with crusty bread and butter.

w.how: Line a 23cm tart tin with sweet shortcrust and chill 20 minutes. Beat 100g soft butter with 100g caster sugar, then 2 eggs and 100g almond meal. Spread in the case and press in 300g blackberries. Bake at 180C for 40 minutes until golden and set. Cool, dust with icing sugar and serve with thick cream.

d.how: Pour 1.5L cloudy apple juice into a pot with 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 whole cloves, a few strips of orange peel and 1 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 15 minutes without boiling so the spices come through. Strain out the cloves. Ladle into mugs and float a thin apple slice in each.
